page: Microsoft Azure E4-2ads_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine utilizing a constrained vCPU configuration. Built upon Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance runs on an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked at 4.5 GHz with 32 MB of L3 cache. It allocates 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core with multithreading enabled. The instance provides 32.0 GB of system RAM, resulting in an elevated 16.0 GB per vCPU ratio, alongside a local 236 GB NVMe SSD. It does not include GPU acceleration or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results demonstrate a stark contrast between single-threaded efficiency and aggregate multi-threaded throughput. Single-core performance ranks in the top tier, shown by a stress-ng score of 3,678.18, a Geekbench single-core score of 2,792.0, and fast single-threaded gzip compression at 38.9 GB/sec. Modern instruction set extensions like AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16 also support efficient text processing and small-model inference (412.06 tokens/sec prompt processing for 135M parameters). However, due to the 2-vCPU hardware ceiling, multi-core benchmarks such as the PassMark CPU score (5,018.32), Geekbench multi-core (3,628.0), software compilation, and ray tracing fall into the bottom quartile.

The qualitative profile of the E4-2ads_v7 balances high per-thread compute capability and high memory density against low total core count, making it cost-efficient for workloads that are memory-bound rather than compute-bound. It is well-suited for medium-density caching layers, in-memory databases, and applications burdened by per-core software licensing requirements where access to 32 GB of RAM is necessary.
description: Microsoft Azure E4-2ads_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor operating at 4.5 GHz. The configuration provisions 2 dedicated vCPUs (1 physical core with 2 threads), 32.0 GB of RAM, and a local 236 GB NVMe SSD, without GPU acceleration. The instance exhibits top-tier single-threaded performance, recording a Geekbench single-core score of 2,792.0 and single-threaded gzip throughput of 38.9 GB/sec. Conversely, overall multithreaded capacity is constrained by the two-vCPU limit, resulting in low multi-core benchmark rankings. With 16.0 GB of memory per vCPU, this instance offers efficient resource allocation for memory-heavy, low-parallelism workloads such as small in-memory caches, lightweight database engines, and software restricted by per-core software licensing.
